title: State of the Feed — Week of July 20–26, 2026
content_html:
Seven aggregation runs processed 7,364 articles this week, yielding 490 quality articles across eight content categories. News dominated intake at 175 articles, followed by AI-tech at 94 and local coverage at 57. Wellness, science, and climate content represented 50, 48, and 34 articles respectively, with homelab and science fiction comprising the remainder. The dimensional scoring model weighted relevance at 0.55, quality at 0.25, and local signal at 0.20.

Pipeline efficiency maintained a mean noise-to-signal ratio of 2.03 across the week's runs, with individual feed performance ranging from 1.23 to 2.74 articles fetched per one delivered. Two new feeds were integrated: Information Bulletins from BC Wildfire Service and Vancouver Sun, addressing coverage gaps in local and emergency content. One existing feed, LoRaMeshDevices, reported errors during aggregation cycles.

Feed discovery analysis identified three high-scoring candidates for addition: ScienceAlert (68.9), Neuroscience News from ScienceDaily (68.0), and BC Wildfire Service bulletins (66.8). The wildfire service feed has already been integrated; the other two candidates remain pending review for integration into the science category pipeline.

Calibration

KnobOldNewRationale
limits.min_claude_score1820User feedback threshold_sweep shows min_claude_score=20 would cut 28.5% of bad articles while losing only 5.9% of good articles—a favorable trade given the 63.3% overall bad rate. Current value of 18 (raised July 19) is an improvement but insufficient: we're still passing far too many bad articles (band_precision shows even 40-59 composite scores are 54.8% bad). Final feed sizes average 353/run, well above the ~100 target, confirming we have capacity. The previous raises (13→16→18) were conservative steps; user feedback now provides clear evidence to move to the calibration ceiling. This directly addresses the verified quality issue without risking feed scarcity.
